evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 12.20 mg/L at 48.0h dropping to 5.25 mg/L at 48.2h and 4.27 mg/L at 52.0h
Source batches 1-3 maintained DO2 ~9-11 mg/L during 48-52h window, showing divergent receiving behavior
Forward model KEEP: post-decision min DO 1.40 mg/L, 4.8h below 2.0 limit, product mass 183.3 kg
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: min DO 2.22 mg/L, 0h below limit, 231.8 kg product, feasible=true
Forward model combined/increase_air/reduce_feed: min DO 1.74/1.45/1.51 mg/L, all infeasible
Delayed P assays: 0.99 g/L at 36h, 2.89 g/L at 48h — production ongoing but oxygen-limited trajectory
args.rationale: At t=52h the receiving fermentation's DO2 has crashed (~4.3-5.2 mg/L, falling) versus ~10-11 mg/L in all three source batches at comparable age, indicating oxygen demand exceeding transfer capacity. KEEP is projected to violate the 2.0 mg/L minimum for ~4.8h (min ~1.4 mg/L). Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6x feed, 1.15x air) is the only action the source-calibrated forward model deems feasible: minimum DO ~2.22 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, and the highest retained product mass (~232 kg vs ~183 kg under KEEP). It directly cuts oxygen demand via the feed while adding transfer capacity, preserving batch production rather than stopping (zero counted production).
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not receiving-true; the model's transfer multiplier estimate (0.52) and hidden receiving parameters mean actual DO trajectories may differ. Sensitivity members for strong_feed_reduction: 4/5 feasible, min DO range 1.36-3.13 mg/L, product mass 175-623 kg — so a residual risk of still dipping below 2.0 mg/L in unfavorable realizations. Delayed assay availability (4h lag) limits real-time state knowledge; if DO2 continues falling faster than modeled, further escalation would be warranted.
